warnings: ECC_MAC_PJ_OVERRIDE=0.23 pJ per MAC (M. Horowitz, 'Computing's energy problem (and what we can do about it)', ISSCC 2014, Fig. 1.1.9 'Rough energy costs for various operations in 45nm 0.9V'): the Compute category was rescaled in the evaluator from the ERT's 0.23000 pJ/MAC to MACs x this value. Every ECC PERCENTAGE in this file has a different denominator from the primary result; no saved pJ changed. ECC_OPT_METRIC=edp: a cheaper MAC can move the mapping optimum, and the mapper was NOT re-run (it prices MACs from the ERT) -- a fixed-mapping result
approximations: Interconnect energy uses Timeloop's Legacy network model with one shared 45nm wire constant and per-architecture switching terms (archs/_shared/noc.yaml); hop distance is derived by Timeloop from each level's Accelergy area. The recon arm scales the WEIGHT share of NoC energy by K/N like the other on-chip categories.
exact stored codeword count x measured DRAM refetch factor; parity + message padding; rounded up to whole DRAM words once

The baseline's DRAM cost is a PER-BIT PRICE, not extra traffic: it reads the same weight bits as the embedded arm (the decoder is on the DRAM die, so parity is corrected there and never crosses the datapath) and pays 22 pJ/bit against 20 for the bigger, indexed array (x1.1000 on the whole DRAM category, weights, inputs and outputs alike -- a per-bit cost is a property of the device, not of a dataspace). The parity accounting on this result is the array-SIZE evidence for that price, not an energy term; it charges no pJ. E_background and E_refresh grow with the array and are not modelled.

complete codeword read: every bit of every DRAM weight read that Timeloop counts is billed, message and embedded parity alike, and no K/N reduction is applied at DRAM; no external parity; physical DRAM words are ESTIMATED as bits / word rounded up once at the end (bit-proportional -- Timeloop bills per 8-bit scalar); the final chunk's tail padding is reported, not charged, as for the baseline

ECC codec (decode/correction) energy is OUTSIDE this comparison: it is charged to neither arm (Task 2: do not silently change ECC codec energy). Note that the arms would decode different numbers of codewords -- the baseline packs whole weights into a separately stored codeword, the embedded layout cuts the weight bit stream itself -- so a codec cost would not cancel; it is simply not costed until a characterised codec energy is adopted. ECC_DECODE affects the sweep figures only.
This is a fixed-mapping, DRAM-only comparison. It credits no on-chip saving to the embedded arm and makes no inference-accuracy claim about overwriting weight LSBs with parity.

layout.layout_meaning: the MSB-first weight bit stream is cut into fixed n-bit codewords; weights straddle codeword boundaries; the parity overwrites the lowest-significance positions; storage is weight_bits per weight with no external parity

parity_significance.rule: per chunk, the n-k parity bits overwrite the positions of lowest bit significance (ties: higher chunk index first)

layout_source.pipeline: ECC-CODE-Engine/4-EmbeddingECC/ecc_embed.py -- approach `replace`, chunk_size = message_parity_size (the codeword n); one int8 tensor per call
layout_source.slicing: Input_Embedding/3-Testing/utils/messageSliceBasedOnChunkSize.py -- fixed n-bit chunks over the MSB-first 8-bit weight stream; chunks span weights; only the last chunk is zero-padded
layout_source.encoding: Input_Embedding/3-Testing/implementations/ParityOverwriteByTopWeightsEncode.py -- systematic BCH(n,k) via galois.BCH(n,k).G; the k highest-significance chunk positions are the message, the n-k lowest-significance positions are overwritten with the parity
layout_source.phases: Input_Embedding/3-Testing/implementations/secded_vectorized.py -- the chunk/weight alignment repeats every lcm(n, 8)/n chunks

input_glb + weight_glb + psum_glb.modelled: the stock 128 kB shared_glb split by DATASPACE into 28 kB inputs (8b), 36 kB weights (8b, or q on the reconstruction arm) and 64 kB psums (16b)
input_glb + weight_glb + psum_glb.rationale: The stock file declares datawidth 16 on EVERY level while declaring an 8-bit multiplier, so an 8-bit-weight study charged it twice the DRAM energy per weight. Timeloop allows one datawidth per level, so the shared buffer had to be split to give each dataspace its own. The psum split dates from 2026-09-06; the operand half was split into input_glb and weight_glb on 2026-09-13, for the same one-datawidth reason one level down: a level holding Weights beside Inputs cannot declare the reconstruction arm's q-bit weights without also declaring the input activations to be q bits, and under the default ECC_WEIGHT_CAPACITY_SCOPE=exclusive it is not a weight level at all. Total capacity and word width are unchanged (36 + 28 + 64 = 128 kB).

split_ratio.status: NOT CITED, and there is no paper to cite: this is a reference design. Chosen 2026-09-13 from this design's OWN cached mappings, 53 distinct layer shapes at the 65,536-word shared operand_glb.
split_ratio.measured_demand: summed partition size (the distinct values the level is asked to hold) Weights 8,068,576 = 53.3 %, Inputs 7,064,919 = 46.7 %; refetch (fills / partition) Weights 1.088x, Inputs 1.113x, so at 64 kB shared NEITHER dataspace bound; peak utilized capacity Weights 64,000 words (the fc shape C1280_M1000), Inputs 57,344 (early large-fmap shapes); median Weights 4,320, Inputs 25,056.
split_ratio.rationale: The measured demand is the base (53/47) and the tilt to 56/44 is the dataflow: weights are the resident operand here and this design's low DRAM weight refetch is the quantity the ECC study measures. The tilt is kept to one bank-pair because the counter-argument is real -- the input path has NO PE scratchpad (inputs go GLB -> input_activation_reg, depth 1), so this is the only input reuse level on chip and takes 90 % of the level's reads.
split_ratio.cost: Both halves are smaller than the 64 kB either dataspace could reach before, so fills -- DRAM traffic -- can only RISE on both, and the peak-demand layers re-tile. Not corrected for: that is what a partitioned buffer is.

input_glb + weight_glb + psum_glb.bank_geometry: CHANGED 2026-09-13, and this is where the old claim "bank geometry is unchanged, so per-access energy is the stock number" stopped being true. Splitting one 64 kB array into a 36 kB and a 28 kB one gives CACTI two smaller arrays; recorded, not compensated for. n_banks is 8 on both, so the 16 operand banks are conserved and BOTH levels are priced on the same banking model -- keeping the stock 512-entry bank instead would have meant 9 banks and 7, and `sram_banking` below records that CACTI is called at the next power of two, which would have priced a 36 kB array as 16 banks against a 28 kB array as 8. Entries per bank move instead: 576 and 448.
input_glb + weight_glb + psum_glb.measured_effect: Accelergy at 45nm on this design's own geometry, reference arm (q=8), per 8-bit value so the word widths are comparable -- the pre-split operand_glb (8192 x 64b, 16 banks) read 2.2821 pJ and wrote 2.6656; input_glb (3584 x 64b, 8 banks) reads 1.6305 (-28.6 %) and writes 1.7167 (-35.6 %); weight_glb (768 x 384b after THE WIDTH TABLE, 8 banks) reads 2.1394 (-6.3 %) and writes 2.3074 (-13.4 %). SMALLER ARRAYS ARE CHEAPER PER ACCESS AND PER BIT, not dearer -- the direction CACTI gives for shorter bitlines, and the same direction `sram_banking` below measures for banking. LEAKAGE GOES THE OTHER WAY: two arrays carry two sets of peripherals, so the declared leak rises from 0.0025893 pJ/cycle to 0.0010206 + 0.0020248 = 0.0030454, x1.177. The arm-to-arm spread stays inside THE WIDTH TABLE's 2 % rule: weight_glb reads 102.689 pJ/word at width 384 (q=8) against 101.941 at width 380 (q=5), 0.7 % apart.
input_glb + weight_glb + psum_glb.port_bandwidth: Each of the three levels declares read/write 16 items/cycle, the same uncited reference-design inheritance `onchip_bandwidth` records for every other level in the study, and the same pattern eyeriss_like_wglb follows with three separate GLB levels. The operand path therefore has two 16-item ports where it had one. Stated because the roofline (latency_post) reads these.

mapper_settings.seed_note: timeloop-mapper v4 exposes no random seed; pytimeloop's Mapper spec has no `random_seed` attribute. ECC_MAPPER_SEED is RECORDED so a result says which value was asked for, but it does not make the search deterministic. What does bound it is the thread count and victory condition, both of which are in the fingerprint -- so pin ECC_MAPPER_THREADS for a reproducible run rather than leaving it at 'all cores', which differs per machine.
